firmwares.name: bf-5rh M0 (upstream, unmodified)
firmwares.notes: First-flash build, boots on 5RH10W-V05, all subsystems verified 2026-11-24.

apps.name: ACTLOG
apps.notes: Activity logger: scans programmed channels, logs squelch hits (persistent).
apps.blurb: Unattended activity logger. It scans the radio's programmed channels (about 90 ms per channel, speaker muted) and records every squelch hit — frequency, start time, peak RSSI, duration — to flash memory, where the log survives app exit and power cycles (up to 768 hits).
apps.usage: Leave it running on a shelf or in the car; open the review view (MENU) later to see what was active and when. * + MENU clears the log.

apps.name: CHANMGR
apps.blurb: Channel manager for the radio's programmed memory channels: browse the channel list with names and frequencies, and manage entries without a computer.
apps.usage: Scroll the list to review channels; follow the on-screen keys to edit or clear an entry.

apps.name: FM
apps.blurb: FM broadcast receiver for the 87.5–108 MHz band, using the radio's dedicated FM tuner chip. Tune by hand, step through the band, or seek to the next station; up to 30 FM presets are kept in the radio's FM channel list.
apps.usage: Open FM from the launcher, then use the arrow keys to tune/step and MENU to seek.

apps.name: FOXHUNT
apps.notes: Direction-finding helper: big RSSI readout, peak hold, bearing samples.
apps.blurb: Direction-finding helper for hunting a transmitter on foot: a big live RSSI readout in dBm with a bar graph and decaying peak marker, plain-language guidance (STRONG/WARM/WEAK with body-block and attenuation prompts), and up to 8 bearing samples you can snapshot as you move.
apps.usage: Walk the area watching the readout and peak; press MENU at each bearing point to save a sample, and # toggles a beeper whose rate rises with signal strength.

apps.name: RPTBOOK
apps.notes: Repeater book: Preston's programmed channels as a tuneable directory (accepts injected ZIP data).
apps.blurb: A tuneable repeater directory baked from Preston's own programmed channels (165 entries, parsed from his pre-flash backup): names, frequencies and tones, read-only. It also accepts an injected data block (the ZIP-code flow), so a future web page can load repeaters near any ZIP without rebuilding the app.
apps.usage: Scroll to an entry and press MENU to tune it exactly in-app; EXIT after a tune lands the standby VFO on the entry's RX frequency.

apps.name: SATELLITE
apps.notes: Satellite pass prediction + tracking (needs satellite table + observer position).
apps.blurb: Amateur satellite helper in three parts: a satellite list, pass prediction, and a tracking view with Doppler-aware tuning. It needs its satellite table loaded into the app-data region and an observer position in settings before it can predict passes — until then it opens to an empty list.
apps.usage: After the table and observer position are set, pick a satellite to see its next passes and open the track view during a pass.

apps.name: SCANQT
apps.notes: CTCSS/DCS tone hunter on the current channel.
apps.blurb: Tone hunter: sits on the current channel and works out which CTCSS/DCS tone an incoming signal is using, so you can program the right tone for a repeater or simplex contact.
apps.usage: Tune to an active signal, open SCANQT, and let it test tones while the other station transmits.

apps.name: SEARCH
apps.blurb: Frequency search: sweeps a range and collects the frequencies where the squelch opens into a found list you can step through and tune.
apps.usage: Start a search over the range you care about, then step through the found frequencies.

apps.name: SETTINGS
apps.blurb: On-radio editor for the firmware's settings, in three groups (menu, radio, system): squelch, band lock, backlight, side-key functions, boot text and more — the same 168-byte settings record the web CPS reads and writes.
apps.usage: Pick a group, scroll to a setting, and edit it in place; changes are written to the radio's settings storage.

apps.name: SPECTRUM
apps.blurb: Live spectrum sweep around the current frequency: samples signal strength across a span and draws it as a bar graph, so you can see band activity, find busy spots, and spot noise at a glance.
apps.usage: Tune near the band you care about, open SPECTRUM, and watch the sweep; stronger signals draw taller bars.

apps.name: WXPANEL
apps.notes: NOAA weather panel: 7 WX channels with per-channel RSSI + auto-strongest.
apps.blurb: NOAA weather radio panel: lists all seven WX channels (162.400–162.550 MHz) with a measured signal strength for each, and automatically tunes the strongest one — handy for checking which weather transmitter covers your spot.
apps.usage: Open WXPANEL and it samples all seven channels and lands on the strongest; use UP/DOWN + MENU to tune manually, * re-runs the auto-scan.
